text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Two Americans face charges of attempting to defraud Bank Bumiputra Malaysia Bhd of $600 million involving fraudulent time drafts.
-- Police form a five-member team headed by state criminal investigation department chief to investigate log smuggling activities in Sabah state.
-- U.S. ambassador Johan Mallot says bilateral relations between the United States and Malaysia have been on a definite upswing since 1994 and will likely to continue in that direction.
-- The Immigration Department detains four maids during a house-to-house check to curb the employment of illegal immigrants in the country.
-- The Sabah state government wants a stop to all transhipment of logs to the state, including those from countries allowing the export of the commodity such as Papua New Guinea and New Zealand.
